headline: TCI Express: Substantial Acquisition Disclosure under SEBI Takeover Code
sum: TCI Express Limited has filed a Regulation 29(2) disclosure with NSE, signalling a substantial acquisition of shares triggering takeover code obligations. The intimation confirms an acquirer has crossed a mandatory disclosure threshold, requiring publication of detailed shareholding and intent details.
implication: Regulation 29(2) disclosure is a gateway event: it signals intent to acquire control or a de facto control trigger (≥25% or creeping acquisition), and mandates that the acquirer now file a formal takeover bid or open offer within the statutory window—a critical milestone for deal counsel to map offer mechanics, pricing, and minority-protection conditions.
detail: TCI Express Limited, a listed logistics and express distribution company, has notified NSE of a substantial acquisition of shares under SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeover) Regulations, 2011. The Regulation 29(2) disclosure is the first mandatory step when an acquirer crosses 25% of voting capital or accumulates shares in a manner triggering creeping acquisition thresholds. The filing does not yet reveal the acquirer's identity, quantum, or price; those details are typically published in the formal takeover bid document (Form 4 / 5) filed with SEBI within two days of the disclosure. The company and the stock exchange have been notified; further disclosures to shareholders and the public are imminent.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeover) Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 29(2)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure when acquirer crosses 25% threshold or triggers creeping acquisition limits; triggers duty to open offer within 60 days.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeover) Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 3, 4 & 5
framework.note: Definition of acquirer, control, and substantial acquisition; determines who must file and what thresholds apply.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeover) Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 10 & 11
framework.note: Open offer mechanics, offer price (minimum), and conditions precedent to completion.
Postal ballot and shareholder approval for related-party transactions and change of control; may apply if acquirer is connected to TCI management.
Disclosure of material events including substantial acquisition; ensures continuous market transparency.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992 — Section 11(4)
framework.note: Regulator's powers to regulate takeover bids and protect minority shareholders.
If TCI Express is in financial stress, acquisition may intersect with IBC resolution frameworks.

conditions: Acquirer must file formal takeover bid (Form 4 or 5) with SEBI within two trading days of Regulation 29(2) disclosure
Open offer must be made within 60 days to acquire up to 20% additional shares from public shareholders
Offer price to be determined by SEBI-mandated valuation or negotiated minimum floor set by regulation
Clearances from FDI/FIPB (if foreign acquirer) and CCI (if deal size warrants merger notification)
approvals: SEBI: Form 4/5 takeover bid filing and clearance
Stock Exchange (NSE/BSE): Listing compliance and trading halt if necessary
Shareholder vote: if acquisition triggers related-party thresholds or change-of-control provisions
Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB): if acquirer is foreign entity exceeding FDI caps
CCI: merger notification if combined assets or revenues exceed thresholds under Competition Act, 2010
structure.novel: Regulation 29(2) disclosure itself is a transparency innovation—it flags intent early and prevents clandestine creeping acquisitions, but reveals no detail until the full takeover document is filed, creating a 24–48-hour information asymmetry that counsel must manage carefully.

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeover) Regulations, 2011
triggers.note: The 25% threshold or creeping acquisition trigger under Regulation 3 forces the disclosure event and mandates public open offer within 60 days.
If combined turnover of acquirer and TCI Express exceeds ₹2,500 cr (or other CCI thresholds), prior CCI approval required before completion.

triggers.law: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) & FDI Regulations
triggers.note: If acquirer is non-resident, acquisition is subject to FIPB/DPIIT foreign investment caps and repatriation rules for the sector.

triggers.law: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 44(1) and Schedule I
triggers.note: Change of control may constitute 'transfer of undertaking' requiring Board/shareholder approval and regulatory clearance in regulated sectors (TCI Express is in logistics, generally open).

firms.side: Acquirer (counsel identity not disclosed in primary filing)
firms.note: Takeover code filings do not mandate disclosure of acquirer's counsel at the Regulation 29(2) stage; full legal team details typically emerge in the Form 4/5 bid document.

firms.side: TCI Express Limited (counsel not stated in intimation)
firms.note: Company counsel role will expand post-bid: advising on offer response, fairness opinions, and negotiation strategy.

timeline.t: Regulation 29(2) disclosure filed with NSE (and BSE); public intimation issued by TCI Express.
Acquirer's formal takeover bid document (Form 4 or 5) due to SEBI within two trading days of Regulation 29(2) disclosure.
SEBI reviews and clears bid document; company publishes detailed offer details and shareholder defence memorandum.
Open offer window closes (within 60 days of bid filing); acquirer's acquisition of up to additional 20% completes or lapses.
